Name: Joshua Henderson

Experiance.Title: Application Developer

This required working across the full stack, with SPFx and React on the front end and C# Azure Functions and PowerShell behind it. I developed both customer-facing features and the internal tooling our operations and support teams relied on, while working closely with client-facing internal users to keep implementation matched to business need.

Drove AI adoption across a five-developer team, leading to improved QA, detailed documentation and consistent code across projects.

Designed and built the interface for an internal administration application (React 19, TypeScript, Vite, Azure Static Web Apps), which provides a single pane of glass to administer SharePoint webhooks across 30+ distinct tenants.

Designed and built a Power Automate system that files incoming coal-analysis documents automatically — parsing lab emails to identify the vessel or rail car, tagging and filing them into SharePoint, with a weekly sweep that flags anything unmatched for review.
Administered hybrid Azure AD and on-premises Active Directory; built and managed the VMware and Nutanix environment; managed on- and off-premises backup with Veeam and Nutanix Xi Leap.
Implemented MFA, an SSO-secured password manager, a ticketing system, and the company's first IT documentation set on a quarterly review cycle.
Tracked and responded to incoming threats by working closely with the external NOC and SOC.

Projects.Title: Digital Resume
Projects.Description: A single-page resume built as a React 19 and TypeScript application and deployed to Cloudflare Workers. Every section renders from one typed JSON document, so updating my experience, skills or recommendations is a data change rather than a code change. I built it to keep my resume current in one place, and to have somewhere to work with the parts of the stack I do not reach for at work.
Highlights: Data-driven throughout: one typed JSON document feeds the hero, experience, skills, projects, recommendations and contact sections.
Skills are derived from the job history rather than maintained separately, so the tag list cannot drift out of date.
Each section is its own component, with scroll-triggered reveals built on IntersectionObserver instead of an animation library.
Styled with Tailwind 4 and shadcn/ui, with light and dark themes and a layout that works from phone width up.
Built with Vite and deployed to Cloudflare Workers with Wrangler; the build type-checks the whole app before it ships.

Projects.Title: HDSN-TECH Home Lab
Projects.Tagline: A production-style network I run at home
Projects.Description: A self-hosted lab I have run and rebuilt for about a decade, and where most of what I know about networking, virtualisation and Linux was actually learned. It is a segmented pfSense network on a Proxmox hypervisor, with Active Directory, a NAS, a Docker host and a monitoring stack, all kept to the same standards I would apply at work: VLAN isolation, scheduled backups, alerting and documentation.
Highlights: pfSense firewall routing six VLANs — infrastructure, security, guest, IoT, game and a second site segment — with the camera, guest and IoT networks isolated from the server network.
Proxmox hypervisor hosting the firewall, domain controllers and media VMs, migrated off an ageing VMware ESXi host without losing services.
Windows Server Active Directory domain with two domain controllers across sites, running DNS, Kerberos, LDAP and SMB.
TrueNAS/FreeNAS storage serving SMB shares, with configuration exports and scheduled application backups archived off the host.
Ubuntu Docker host running n8n, Portainer and a handful of self-built services, published selectively over Tailscale rather than open ports.
An n8n workflow polls every service on a five minute schedule and sends a Pushover alert the moment one stops answering.
Whole estate documented from live nmap scans — a device inventory, a network diagram and per-service runbooks kept in version control.

Projects.Title: PZ Server Manager
Projects.Tagline: A web control panel for my game servers
Projects.Description: A Node and Express web app that runs beside my Project Zomboid servers in Docker and gives them the management interface they never shipped with. It began as a throwaway, vibe-coded experiment to stop me SSHing into the host every time a server needed a restart or a mod, and turned into the tool I now run everything through: it discovers every server on the host, streams their logs, edits their configuration and tells me on my phone when something happens. Its growth is also what forced the engineering into it, the crash handling, the config validation and the notification plumbing all came from running the quick version for real and finding where it broke.
Highlights: Single-page UI over a REST API, with dashboard, mods, players, logs and settings views, running as its own docker container alongside the game servers.
Live log view streamed over server-sent events straight from the container, with filtering, pause and severity colouring.
Mod installs driven through SteamCMD, including whole Steam Workshop collections resolved from the public collection endpoint, with download progress parsed out of the server log.
Servers are discovered by cross-referencing Docker bind mounts rather than being hardcoded, so a new server appears in the picker under its own live name with no config edit.
Push and Discord notifications for crashes, low disk, completed downloads and player join, leave, death and kick events, read from the game logs by byte offset so nothing replays after a restart.
Full configuration editor covering every key in the server ini, plus raw access to the sandbox Lua file rather than a fragile parser for it.

Debugged the parts that only break in production: a blocking child process that killed in-flight downloads on redeploy, and a request handler that silently fell back to the wrong server on a stale selection.

Recomendations.Name: Jake
Recomendations.Title: Senior Architect
Recomendations.Relationship: Worked with Joshua on the same team
Recomendations.Text:
I worked closely with Joshua for more than two years at VPO, collaborating with him on numerous application development and cloud engineering initiatives. He consistently impressed me with his exceptional work ethic, technical curiosity, humility, and dedication. Joshua is the kind of engineer who can quickly master an unfamiliar problem, develop a thoughtful solution, document it thoroughly, and stay engaged until the work is done correctly.

One of the best examples was our construction drawing issuance system, a particularly complex and demanding project. The system began with a PowerShell-based solution that Joshua authored. As its requirements evolved, he helped guide me through modernizing it into an Azure Durable Functions architecture. I developed much of the Azure Functions implementation, but Joshua remained an invaluable partner throughout the process, helping us overcome difficult technical challenges and carrying forward the deep knowledge he had built through the original system. His combination of technical ability, ownership, and willingness to collaborate made a significant difference.

Joshua also stands out in how effectively he uses AI for rapid prototyping and software development. He approaches new tools with curiosity and sound judgment, using them to accelerate delivery while still producing well-considered, maintainable solutions.

Above all, Joshua is dependable, passionate about his work, and continually learning. He consistently exceeds expectations, and I would work with him again without hesitation. I strongly recommend him to any organization seeking a dedicated software or cloud engineer who will make an immediate and lasting contribution.

He led developer forums that kept the team aligned, encouraged knowledge sharing, and helped us all find meaningful ways to incorporate AI into our development workflows.

One of Josh's greatest strengths is his ability to quickly become productive with new technologies. He has a natural ability to learn, understand, and apply new concepts without losing sight of sound engineering principles and maintainable architecture.

Beyond his technical abilities, Josh is the kind of teammate everyone wants in their corner. When a team member needs help, he is always one of the first to lend a hand. He brings a collaborative attitude, shares his knowledge freely, and genuinely wants to see the entire team succeed.

Josh is an exceptional developer, a strong technical leader, and a teammate I would be excited to work with again.
